title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Diabetes Risk Prediction Across Demographically Heterogeneous Hospital Nodes
abstract: Background and Objective. Diabetes risk models achieve strong discrimination on centralised cohorts, but centralisation is constrained by privacy regulation, and models trained at a single site risk demographic bias and miscalibration. We evaluate whether federated learning (FL) can deliver diabetes risk prediction that is simultaneously generalisable, equitable, calibrated, and privacy-preserving across demographically heterogeneous hospital nodes, without centralising patient data. Methods. NHANES 2013-2020 (n = 15,650) was partitioned into three nodes representing young-urban, elderly-rural, and mixed-metropolitan populations. Four FL aggregation strategies - FedAvg, FedProx (mu = 0.1), FedNova, and SCAFFOLD - were trained over 50 communication rounds and validated externally on BRFSS 2020-2022 (n = 1,282,897). A shared global scaler prevented cross-node data leakage. To separate the effect of federation from architecture, a centralised DiabetesNet with identical architecture was trained on the full NHANES pool and, in a sensitivity analysis, on the matched federated subset (n = 11,906). Fairness was measured as the AUC gap between young (18-39) and elderly (>=60) respondents; post-hoc calibration (Platt, isotonic, temperature scaling) and differential privacy (DP-SGD) were also evaluated. Results. FedAvg achieved the highest external AUC, 0.757 [95% CI 0.756-0.758], exceeding the centralised XGBoost baseline (0.700 [0.698-0.701]) by 0.057 and the architecture-matched centralised DiabetesNet (0.749 [0.748-0.750]). Its generalisation gap (internal minus external AUC) was 0.031, versus 0.052 for the full-pool centralised DiabetesNet - a 40% reduction; a sample-matched sensitivity analysis (gap = 0.024) indicated that data composition, not federation alone, accounts for part of this advantage. FedAvg reduced the elderly-young fairness gap from 0.069 (centralised XGBoost) to 0.054, a 21.7% within-study improvement, and isotonic recalibration reduced expected calibration error (ECE) from 0.276 to 0.001 without loss of discrimination. Under DP-SGD, utility collapsed to AUC around 0.50 at epsilon <= 5 and recovered to 0.769 at epsilon = 10; however, Opacus RDP accounting returned epsilon_actual = infinity at that budget, so epsilon = 10 identifies a utility floor rather than a formal privacy guarantee at the per-node sizes used (n around 3,000-4,500). Conclusions. Across four axes of clinical deployability, federated diabetes screening matched or exceeded centralised baselines while keeping patient data local. Relative to a sample-matched centralised model, federation's advantage rests less on the generalisation gap itself than on privacy preservation, improved elderly fairness, and feasibility under regulatory constraints. The framework is a validated proof-of-concept; prospective evaluation in genuinely independent multi-site cohorts remains the essential next step. Preprint - not peer reviewed. Submitted for publication.

title: Emotions in Hydrology
abstract: Emotion analysis, primarily employed in social media text analysis, holds significant potential for unveiling patterns within large-scale scientific corpora. To explore this, I analyzed a corpus comprising 7.36 million sentences sourced from leading hydrological journals, including Water Resources Research and Journal of Hydrology, spanning years from 2010 to 2025. Utilizing emotion analysis coupled with unsupervised clustering, this analysis aimed to automatically track the prevailing progresses and limitations within the hydrological community across years. For instance, a progression in hydrological modeling from simple to hybrid models, a shift from single to integrated observation systems, and the increasing application of machine learning techniques were observed. The data extracted from the negative emotion, however, suggests a more worrying reality. Despite technological advancements, concerns regarding extreme hydrological event predictions, water resource monitoring, and simulation accuracy persist. Ultimately, while hydrological technology has advanced, the water crisis continues to worsen. Addressing this crisis necessitates breaking the negative feedback loop between human activities and water resources. Emotion analysis in hydrology allows us to examine the complex water-human relationship from a historical and broad perspective. It also serves to identify the tangible contribution the field has made toward restoring this relationship and informs prospective future efforts.

title: OrbiTrack: Ball Tracking Robotic Car
abstract: This paper offers a comprehensive review of orbitrack, and open-source robot that is designed to make robotics accessible, inexpensive and easy for early people. Orbitrack enables the user to locate the objects and maneuver towards them, also aids them in other concepts such as IOT and Computer Vision. This review contains several features of orbitrack, such as the system implementation, control of the robot with the help of live camera feeds, and choice of balls with the help of computer vision. The orbitrack software remains compatible with the work, and the python application that runs on PC is different. Comprehensive guidelines are given on how to make hand tracking, robot control and ball-choice robot projects, which illustrate the potential of Orbitrack as an educational resource and tool of robotics and IOT activity.

title: Source-Aware Recovery and Security Bounds in Temporal-Mode Quantum Communication
abstract: We analyze a temporal-mode extension of the two-way LM05 quantum communication primitive, in which a message block is encoded into a fixed-weight binary occupation vector (the support) alongside classical ordering information. We demonstrate that applying an independent-slot recovery model to this correlated source is fundamentally inconsistent. For an ideal erasure channel, we derive the exact maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) recovery probability, showing that source-aware decoding outperforms independent guessing by orders of magnitude. We extend this analysis to a realistic threshold-detector model, quantifying the degradation caused by dark counts and inefficiency. Furthermore, we clarify the quantum-classical information split: in the ideal single-photon limit, preparation averaging renders Eve's state independent of the support, yielding zero Holevo information. We establish conditional security bounds using entropic uncertainty relations and identify photon-number-splitting as the primary practical vulnerability. These results provide a rigorous source-aware recovery benchmark and define the physical conditions under which the quantum layer offers a key-consumption advantage over classical constant-weight coding.

title: Maintenance-Coupled Inquiry Control Directs Damage-Relevant Evidence Acquisition and Improves Causal Repair in Artificial Agents
abstract: Artificial agents that execute externally specified tasks should be distinguished from inquiry systems that alter what they investigate in response to their own internal condition. This frozen confirmatory study tests whether a designer-specified maintenance signal aligned with damaged internal components changes evidence allocation, causal diagnosis, and repair in causal microworlds. Across 72 unused confirmatory seeds (30000–30071), the package contains 576 primary and 432 ablation runs, with complete replay for all 288 actual/yoked traces. Actual need increased damage-target active sensing relative to yoked need by 0.1173 (95% CI [0.0722, 0.1632]; predefined minimum effect 0.08). Replicated restoration was 41/72 under actual need and 20/72 under yoked need, a difference of 0.2917 (95% CI [0.1667, 0.4167]). Neutral-world false repair under actual need was 0/72, with a one-sided 95% upper bound of 0.0408 below the predefined 0.05 safety threshold. The common-decoder replicated-restoration difference was 0.2778 (95% CI [0.1528, 0.4028]). The supported claim concerns a functional pathway from maintenance-state correspondence to evidence allocation and downstream causal repair within a causal microworld. This study does not demonstrate constitutive autonomy or endogenous normativity. Internal variables, damage, repair, observation budget, and intervention vocabulary were externally designed. Improvement in internal state is not equivalent to a correct causal explanation. no_bridge and independent validation are distinct mechanisms. Failure analyses performed after confirmatory adjudication remain descriptive and post hoc. The record includes English and Japanese manuscripts, supplementary materials, the byte-identical public release archive, its checksum, the frozen confirmatory protocol, reproducibility instructions, citation metadata, content inventory, checksum manifest, and license/rights documentation. AI-generated output was not treated as a primary source or scientific evidence. title: Does ChatGPT Reconstruct a Company into a Different Company? The Risk of Losing Corporate Specificity in Generative AI Sales Adoption
abstract: Version 1:Japanese-language edition Japanese-language edition(Version 1). 本ホワイトペーパーは、約110ページで構成される原典技術版をもとに、主要な問題構造、営業業務シミュレーション、導入前評価項目、防御ワークフローを、企業の経営者、営業責任者、AI導入担当者向けに分かりやすく簡略化・再構成した日本語版である。 原典技術版では、GPT-5.6における出力再構成、局所修正後の全体再解釈、テンプレートへの再収束、条件保持の不安定性について、画像観測、比較検証、評価基準、実験設計を含めて詳細に検討している。本ホワイトペーパーでは、その中から営業業務への生成AI導入に直接関係する論点を抽出し、企業固有性の消失リスクとして整理した。 対象となるのは、単純な誤回答や情報漏えいだけではない。顧客条件、製造・品質部門の判断、未確定事項、承認範囲、企業固有の約束の仕方が、修正、要約、整文、一文修正の過程で、自然で汎用的な営業テンプレートへ再構成される可能性である。 本稿では、架空企業「二光精機」と医療機器向けチタン精密部品の想定案件を用い、顧客の希望と企業の確約、「検討可能」と「対応可能」、品質要求と品質保証、将来計画と現時点の能力が、長い対話と修正工程の後まで区別して保持されるかを検証する。 また、一文のみの局所修正が文書全体の再解釈を引き起こし、修正対象外の条件、部門権限、技術的留保、ブランドコアを変化させる構造を示す。さらに、AI出力が人間承認、顧客送信、CRM登録、製造条件化を通過することで、単なる下書きから組織の正式情報へ変わる事故経路を整理する。 防御策として、案件コア台帳、会話外の確定条件表、承認済み版管理、条件再注入、生成後の逆照合、ブランド保持ゲート、全文差分確認、停止基準、確定版からの再構築を組み合わせた第2世代防御ワークフローを提示する。 詳細な理論、画像観測、評価基準、実験設計、および検証結果については、約110ページの原典技術版を参照されたい。 本稿の中心的な問いは、処理が完了したかではない。 その会社が、その会社のまま処理されたか。 Version 2:English-language edition English-language edition (Version 2), translated from the Japanese Version 1. This white paper is a simplified and reorganized version of the approximately 110-page original technical edition. It extracts the principal risk structure, sales-operation simulation, pre-deployment evaluation criteria, and defensive workflow and presents them in a form intended for executives, sales managers, and enterprise AI deployment teams. The original technical edition provides a detailed examination of output reconstruction in GPT-5.6, whole-output reinterpretation after local revisions, reconvergence toward stable templates, and instability in condition preservation. It includes image-based observations, comparative testing, evaluation criteria, and experimental design. This white paper extracts the elements most directly relevant to the introduction of generative AI into sales operations and reorganizes them as the risk of losing corporate specificity. The concern is not limited to incorrect answers or information leakage. Customer conditions, manufacturing and quality judgments, unresolved matters, approval boundaries, and the company-specific way of making commitments may be reconstructed into natural, reusable, and generic sales templates through revision, summarization, polishing, and one-sentence editing. Using the fictional company Nikko Seiki and a simulated inquiry involving a titanium precision component for a medical-device manufacturer, the paper examines whether distinctions such as customer request versus company commitment, open for consideration versus available, quality requirement versus quality guarantee, and future plan versus current capability remain preserved after extended dialogue and repeated revisions. The paper also shows how a local one-sentence revision may trigger reinterpretation of the entire document, altering conditions, departmental authority, technical reservations, and the brand core outside the intended revision target. It further identifies the pathway through which AI output moves from a draft to official organizational information through human approval, customer communication, CRM registration, and conversion into manufacturing conditions. As a defensive framework, the paper proposes a Second-Generation Defensive Workflow combining a case-core register, confirmed-condition tables maintained outside the conversation, approved-version management, condition reinjection, reverse verification, a brand-preservation gate, full-document difference checks, stopping criteria, and reconstruction from an approved version. For the complete theoretical framework, image-based observations, evaluation criteria, experimental design, and detailed findings, readers should refer to the approximately 110-page original technical edition. title: When Intelligence Fools Itself: Exploration under Corrupted Feedback in LLM Agents
abstract: LLM agents learn to use tools through closed-loop interaction: propose an action, observe feedback, adapt. This capability is fundamentally reasoning-driven rather than memory-driven—we show that anonymizing a tool’s operators (making them unmemorizable) leaves performance unchanged, while removing feedback collapses it. However, reliability depends critically on the quality of the feedback signal. We construct two controlled environments (an anonymized image-processing tool and an anonymized text-processing tool, 13 operators each) with deterministic ground truth, and systematically study agent exploration under corrupted feedback —metric blind spots and partial-solution traps that produce genuine numerical improvement without approaching the true goal. Our findings: (1) under corrupted feedback, intelligent exploration strategies are systematically deceived—their direction judgments become accelerators along wrong paths—while random strategies are immune by virtue of having no direction; (2) the sign of every strategy is set by one environmental variable, perception (whether the agent can see its input): in the perception-less image environment, temperature rescues (+11%) and analogy-mixed parallel search excels (+23 pp over pure parallel), because the agent is in a hallucination state—it confidently believes false signals it cannot verify; in the perception-rich text environment both hurt (−19%, −31 pp) because reasoning is grounded, and parallel search wins (+6 pp); (3) “bottlenecks” are identifiable in hindsight (learned detector AUC 0.96+, cross-environment) but not predictable in advance (early-step prediction AUC 0.86); (4) a detection-then-retry pipeline reaches the oracle upper bound of unconditional double-runs (image: 56% vs. 39% baseline; text: 88% vs. 63%), with the retry antidote selected by bottleneck type—randomness for trap-ensnared deadlock, parallelism for combinatorial under-coverage; (5) generation–execution decoupling (cold-temperature analogy candidate pool + mechanical execution) bypasses false-signal interception entirely, achieving one-shot perfect solutions where all prior modes required 6–9 steps of trial and error. We conclude with a unified “hallucination framework”: tool-learning bottleneck management is an engineering trade-off between exploration efficiency and accuracy, where perception determines whether the agent is reasoning or hallucinating—and therefore whether antidotes (temperature, analogy) help or hurt. Intelligence belongs on the generation and decision sides; randomness or mechanics on the execution side.

title: Causal Compilation Framework: Preserving Internal Causality in Program Transformation
abstract: This paper introduces the Causal Compilation Framework (CCF), a novel compilation paradigm that addresses the limitations of traditional compilers in the era of data-driven systems, artificial intelligence, and safety-critical applications. While conventional compilers rely solely on observational equivalence (ensuring the source and target programs yield identical final outputs), CCF shifts compilation to causal preservation. By establishing a formal theory of Program Causal Graphs (PCGs), a Causal Intermediate Representation (CIR), and causal-aware optimization passes, CCF guarantees that the internal mechanics, variable dependencies, and directional logic of the computation remain intact during transformation. This work outlines the theoretical foundations, framework architecture, and correctness theorems for causal compilation, paving the way for transparent, robust, and auditable software execution.

title: AI-Based Regional Bangla Speech to Standard Bangla and English Translation System
abstract: This dataset contains 5,200 WAV audio files with Bangla regional speech transcripts. The data is prepared to support machine learning and natural language processing research, especially Bangla automatic speech recognition, regional dialect identification, transcript normalization, and translation-based language analysis. The dataset represents spoken Bangla from eight district-based regional categories: Barishal, Chittagong, Habiganj, Narail, Narsingdi, Rangpur, Sylhet, and Tangail. Each district category contains 650 audio files. The dataset is balanced across all eight districts, resulting in a total of 5,200 audio samples. The original dataset is divided into training, validation, and testing sets. For each district, 520 files are used for training, 65 files are used for validation, and 65 files are used for testing. This creates a total split of 4,160 training files, 520 validation files, and 520 testing files. The file naming convention follows a district-wise serial format: district_serial.wav. For example, Barishal files are named from barishal_0001.wav to barishal_0650.wav. The same naming pattern is used for all district categories. The dataset metadata is maintained in spreadsheet form with file names and corresponding regional transcripts. Additional columns such as standard Bangla and English translation may also be included for normalization and translation tasks. The transcripts reflect natural spoken Bangla and may contain regional vocabulary, pronunciation-based spellings, conversational markers, incomplete sentences, fillers, and code-mixed words. These characteristics make the dataset useful for studying real-world speech and dialect variation in Bangla. Since the data is based on speech, careful transcript verification and audio-transcript alignment are recommended before model training.

title: OmniEdit-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Instruction-based Video Editing
abstract: Instruction-based video editing (IVE) is an emerging field with broad applications, yet evaluating editing models remains challenging. Existing benchmarks suffer from two major limitations: limited task coverage inherited from image editing, which overlooks video-specific dimensions, and inadequate metrics that fail to measure instruction fidelity, allowing incorrect edits to receive high scores due to strong visual priors from the original video. To address these issues, we introduce a comprehensive and structured benchmark for IVE. Our benchmark decomposes editing tasks into multiple video-specific dimensions, including spatial, temporal, audio, and reference-based editing, extending beyond conventional frame-level evaluation. It also distinguishes explicit and implicit instructions and incorporates reasoning-based scenarios to better reflect real-world requirements. Furthermore, we propose an evaluation framework that assesses editing quality from four complementary dimensions: accuracy, preservation, realism, and consistency, using both human judgments and state-of-the-art vision-language models. To emphasize instruction fidelity, we introduce an accuracy-aware penalty mechanism that conditions other scores on accuracy, preventing visually plausible but incorrect edits from receiving inflated evaluations. Extensive experiments on representative open-source and commercial models show that current IVE models remain far from satisfactory. OmniEdit-Bench provides a comprehensive and reliable testbed for evaluating instruction-based video editing and offers insights into future research directions.

title: ADAPTIVE LEARNING SYSTEMS FOR PERSONALIZED INSTRUCTION AND ACHIEVEMENT GAP REDUCTION IN DIVERSE CLASSROOM ENVIRONMENTS
abstract: Adaptive Learning Systems (ALS) have emerged as intelligent educational technologies for supporting personalized instruction, learner engagement, and educational equity; however, empirical evidence regarding their effectiveness across diverse classroom environments remains limited. This study evaluated the effectiveness of ALS in improving academic achievement, learner engagement, educational equity, and teacher-supported instructional adaptability. A mixed-methods research design incorporating a quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test control-group approach was employed with 720 students from six educational institutions across a 14-week intervention period. Quantitative data were obtained from curriculum-aligned pre-test and post-test assessments and system-generated learning analytics, while qualitative data were collected through classroom observations and teacher interviews. The experimental group recorded a mean learning gain of 28.6%, compared with 14.3% for the control group. Subject-specific improvements were highest in Mathematics (32.4%), followed by Science (29.1%), English Language (24.7%), and Social Studies (22.9%). Learners in the lowest achievement quartile recorded a 35.8% improvement, while the achievement gap between high- and low-performing learners decreased by 17.6%. Learning analytics indicated increased engagement, with average daily active engagement reaching 32.5 minutes and task completion reaching 87.3%. Teachers also reported improved instructional decision-making through real-time learner analytics. Overall, the findings indicate that ALS can support personalized, inclusive, and data-informed instruction while enhancing learner engagement and pedagogical adaptability across diverse classroom environments.

title: Identity Intelligence: An On-Device Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Architecture Based on Brain-Region-Wise Functional Mapping
abstract: Artificial intelligence today is, in practice, entirely composed of language models. A language model holds a vast body of knowledge and is remarkably good at retrieving and applying it, but it is not an agent that decides for itself what to do and bears the consequences. It has knowledge but no self. This paper proposes Identity Intelligence: an architecture in which the capacity to judge, to remember, to act, and to restrain oneself is itself implemented as an artificial intelligence, separate from the model that holds knowledge. The proposed architecture maps the anatomically and physiologically differentiated functions of human brain regions onto information-processing modules, and attaches a different safety policy to each processing stage on the grounds that the nature of the threat differs from stage to stage. Judgment is performed by the inference of a replaceable reasoning model rather than being bound to any particular model name, and the destinations of judgment are treated as equal, with no destination privileged over another. Memory opens its read path widely while narrowing its write path, so that deletion or alteration of memory by the artificial intelligence itself is structurally impossible. Safety is not a filter appended at the end but is distributed across every layer, and no input exists that can disable it. All processing occurs on the device; even when an external model is used, sensitivity determination and de-identification are completed before any original data leaves the device. The architecture is realised as a working system. It initiates conversation without being prompted, manages the user's schedule and memories, and converses in six languages. As of August 2026 the implementation has been filed with the Korean Intellectual Property Office as fourteen provisional specifications, whose application numbers are listed in the appendix.

title: The Explanation Cost of Fairness: How Bias Mitigation Affects Explanation Faithfulness in Machine Learning Intrusion Detection
abstract: Machine learning intrusion detectors are accurate but opaque, so explainable AI justifies their alerts and bias mitigation evens out detection across imbalanced categories. These are usually studied independently, and whether making a detector fairer changes how faithfully it can be explained is unknown. In an interventional design, we train an unmitigated baseline and three imbalance mitigations on a one-dimensional CNN, an FT-Transformer, and XGBoost, applying class weighting and oversampling to all three and class-weighted focal loss to the neural models. Faithfulness is measured with deletion-based comprehensiveness and sufficiency, before and after each mitigation, per category, on CICIoT2023 and CICIDS2017. Bias mitigation affects faithfulness unevenly. On the primary dataset, the rare categories most helped gain recall and more faithful explanations, while the largest penalty fell on a category whose detection scarcely changed. XGBoost, explained by exact TreeSHAP, showed no comprehensiveness cost of its own. Among the neural mitigations, focal loss was the most costly, lowering comprehensiveness by up to 0.13 while reducing the recall parity gap by 0.42–0.45, and oversampling was nearly free; this pattern held on both datasets, more weakly on the second, where class weighting and oversampling were not reliably separated. Fairness and interpretability need not be in tension when the mitigation is chosen well, and faithfulness should be evaluated per category whenever a fairness intervention is applied.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation in marketing: an integrative literature review of architectures, applications and strategic implications
abstract: Purpose This study synthesises and critically interprets the emerging literature on retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in marketing. It examines how RAG architectures, applications and governance conditions shape interactive marketing, customer engagement, market sensing and responsible AI deployment. Design/methodology/approach An integrative literature review guided by the SPIDER framework was conducted across Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Google Scholar and Emerald Insight for publications from 2020 to 2025. A final corpus of 25 marketing-relevant RAG studies was analysed through qualitative coding and thematic synthesis. Adjacent peer-reviewed literature on AI in marketing, recommender systems, customer analytics, data-driven marketing capability, AI-augmented co-creation and immersive digital environments was used to contextualise, rather than expand, the primary corpus. Findings Five themes emerge: adaptive and knowledge-graph-enhanced RAG architectures; multilingual, real-time and hyper-personalised customer interaction; intelligent and context-aware retrieval; marketing intelligence and decision support; and robustness, hallucination mitigation and responsible deployment. The review shows that RAG can support retrieval-grounded interaction and market sensing, but evidence is stronger for technical and prototype demonstrations than for longitudinal customer, conversion or strategic outcomes. Responsible deployment requires transparency, privacy safeguards, fairness controls, human oversight and auditable knowledge sources. Originality/value The study advances a marketing-specific interpretation of RAG as a socio-technical marketing capability. It contributes by shifting personalisation from predictive targeting to retrieval-grounded interaction, linking market sensing to dynamic knowledge grounding and positioning governance as intrinsic to the capability rather than a downstream safeguard.

title: Enhancing nighttime object detection via joint-teacher: an unsupervised domain adaptation approach
abstract: Abstract Object detection in nighttime scene presents significant challenges due to domain shifts from daytime environments, primarily caused by insufficient illumination and increased noise. Existing methods often rely on teacher–student frameworks for self-training with pseudo-labels, However, low light and noise increase the difficulty of detection, leading to a significant increase in the positional error between the pseudo-labels and the ground truth. This paper introduces Joint-Teacher, an unsupervised domain adaptation method designed to enhance nighttime object detection. By implementing a student-evaluates-teacher mechanism, we filter reliable pseudo-labels based on regression stability and confidence scores. Additionally, a consistent joint sample strategy is proposed to improve sample allocation accuracy through spatial feature alignment. To simulate real nighttime conditions, a nighttime scene transformation module is designed. Experiments on BDD100K and DWD datasets demonstrate that Joint-Teacher outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average precision of 49.9 on BDD100K and 47.5 on DWD, validating its effectiveness in complex nighttime scene. evidence.title: Enhancing nighttime object detection via joint-teacher: an unsupervised domain adaptation approach
evidence.abstract: Abstract Object detection in nighttime scene presents significant challenges due to domain shifts from daytime environments, primarily caused by insufficient illumination and increased noise. Existing methods often rely on teacher–student frameworks for self-training with pseudo-labels, However, low light and noise increase the difficulty of detection, leading to a significant increase in the positional error between the pseudo-labels and the ground truth. This paper introduces Joint-Teacher, an unsupervised domain adaptation method designed to enhance nighttime object detection. By implementing a student-evaluates-teacher mechanism, we filter reliable pseudo-labels based on regression stability and confidence scores. Additionally, a consistent joint sample strategy is proposed to improve sample allocation accuracy through spatial feature alignment. To simulate real nighttime conditions, a nighttime scene transformation module is designed. Experiments on BDD100K and DWD datasets demonstrate that Joint-Teacher outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average precision of 49.9 on BDD100K and 47.5 on DWD, validating its effectiveness in complex nighttime scene. The code and pretrained models are available at: https://github.com/Jiaquan789/Joint-Teacher .

title: BridgeVLA++: A Data-Efficient, Generalizable, and Memory-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Framework for 3D Manipulation
abstract: Leveraging pre-trained vision-language models (VLMs) to construct vision-language-action (VLA) models has emerged as a promising paradigm for 3D robot manipulation. However, existing 3D VLA methods remain data-hungry, exhibit limited generalization under distribution shifts, and lack explicit memory of past observations. These limitations hinder their application to data-scarce, open-world, and memory-dependent manipulation scenarios. Our previous work, BridgeVLA, improves data efficiency and generalization by preserving the input--output alignment of a pre-trained VLM during 3D action learning: raw point clouds are projected into multi-view images, and intermediate heatmaps are predicted before generating robot actions. In this work, we develop BridgeVLA++ by equipping BridgeVLA with a unified spatio-temporal memory architecture that models persistent spatial context and temporal interaction history. The resulting memory-augmented framework can reason over observation histories while preserving BridgeVLA's data efficiency and generalization capabilities. Extensive experiments show that our framework achieves strong performance on spatial manipulation tasks while exhibiting robust generalization. BridgeVLA++ further achieves state-of-the-art performance on two challenging memory-dependent manipulation benchmarks without sacrificing the data efficiency and generalization of the original BridgeVLA. In addition, BridgeVLA++ performs effectively in bimanual manipulation settings and is validated on an additional real-world robotic platform, demonstrating its scalability across tasks, environments, and robotic platforms. These results establish BridgeVLA++ as a unified 3D vision-language-action framework that simultaneously supports data-efficient learning, robust generalization, and effective memory-aware robot manipulation. Project website: https://bridgevla-plus.github.io/.

title: From Usability to Happiness: Examining the Mediating Role of Flow Experience in Chatbot-Assisted Online Shopping
abstract: AI chatbots are increasingly used by the retailers as a digital marketing tool, helpful to determine the behavioral outcomes of consumers in the form of purchase intentions or buying behavior. The study investigates the impact of chatbot usability on purchase-related happiness in the online retail shopping context, while taking flow experience as a mediator. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, the study has conceptualized chatbot usability as stimulus, flow experience as organism, and purchase-related happiness as emotional response of consumers. Data was collected from online customers having an online shopping experience with chatbot interaction. The sample selection was made using a purposive sampling technique to ensure the relevant sample was selected for the study, since the application of chatbots is at an infancy stage in Pakistan and a limited number of the population has chatbot exposure and buying experience using chatbots. The analysis was performed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that chatbot usability positively influences purchase-related happiness directly and via flow experience. These results confirm the significant positive impact of chatbot usability on purchase-related happiness and also the significant positive mediating impact of flow experience between chatbot usability and purchase-related happiness. The current study advances chatbot usability and purchase-related happiness literature. It also highlights the importance of designing usable chatbots to enhance the affective buying experience of online buyers. Keywords: Chatbot Usability, Flow Experience, Purchase-related Happiness, Stimulus-Organism-Response

title: Computational State Topology: A Topological Framework for Program Analysis and Verification
abstract: Program analysis and verification have long relied on algebraic, logical, and abstract interpretation frameworks. While powerful, these traditional methods often struggle with high-dimensional state spaces and the geometric intuition of complex execution trajectories. This paper introduces Computational State Topology (CST), a novel theoretical framework that models program execution states as topological spaces. By defining program states as points within a structured topological space, denoted as (X_P, tau), and leveraging topological invariants such as Betti numbers (beta_0, beta_1, ..., beta_k), we characterize program behavior, connectivity, error isolation, and algorithmic barriers without relying on traditional exhaustive state-space traversal. This approach bridges the gap between software execution semantics and algebraic topology, establishing a promising mathematical foundation for the next generation of program analysis tools.

title: Augmenting deep learning with hybrid AHA-CO optimization technique for solar radiation prediction
abstract: Precise and reliable Solar Radiation (SR) prediction is an integral part of the thermal systems for renewable energy production. A lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) is designed to generate complex features and a hybrid optimization algorithm combining the artificial hummingbird algorithm (AHA) and Cheetah optimizer (CO), named as AHA-CO, is introduced for Feature selection (FS). The CNN model comprising three convolution layers interlaced by max pooling layers is used to transform inputs to complex features and the AHA-CO is employed to retain only the most informative features without compromising prediction performance and avoid getting stuck in local minima. The developed method is evaluated against 12 individual and three hybrid metaheuristic methods, demonstrating the superior performance of the AHA-CO. Subsequently, the CNN features selected by the AHA-CO are used as input to five regression models. The effectiveness of the SR prediction is assessed on a publicly available dataset. The support vector regression (SVR) model performed the best, forming the CNN-AHA-CO-SVR framework. The results show that the developed framework attained superior performance with 0.0365 mean absolute error, 0.0074 mean squared error, and 0.9251 coefficient of determination, highlighting its robustness and suitability for accurate SR prediction.

title: Lung Lens: Revolutionizing Lung Cancer Detection Through Deep Learning
abstract: Biomedical image diagnosis using deep learning and computer vision has proven to be highly beneficial in providing quick and accurate diagnosis of diseases, matching the accuracy of reliable radiologists. However, deep learning methods alone cannot replace trained medical diagnosis professionals but aim to supplement clinical decision-making. Over the past few decades, machine learning has significantly advanced the field of image analysis. Recent research suggests that deep learning can even surpass human performance in certain visual and auditory recognition tasks, making it a highly suitable approach for medical imaging applications. This study focuses on the development of a web-based application that leverages deep learning and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to accurately detect lung cancer from CT scans. The proposed work introduces a modified Deep CNN architecture tailored for lung cancer identification. In this model, chest CT scan data is segmented into lung-specific features and stored as three-dimensional arrays for improved analysis. The resulting web application demonstrates the potential of deep learning and CNNs to provide precise and reliable lung cancer detection.

title: Chained Recursive Language Models for Multi-Iteration Reasoning
abstract: Long context reasoning in large language models (LLMs) is usually constrained by the fact that a single inference trajectory has to simultaneously explore the context, store intermediate state, verify evidence, and produce the final answer. This becomes particularly difficult in tasks that require extraction, counting, ordering, or multi-hop reasoning, where an early mistake can propagate until the final response. In this work, we propose Chained Recursive Language Models (Chained RLM), an inference-time architecture, in which the same underlying model is called repeatedly as a sequence of fresh reasoning roots. Each root receives the original problem and context, but does not inherit the full conversational history. Instead, it receives a compact plain-text summary, a plain-text blackboard, and some durable task-specific artifacts written by predecessor roots. The motivation is to manage the context by chopping into partial tasks rather than one large inference response; in each staged computation, intermediate artifacts can be inspected, corrected, and extended by a later fresh inference by the same model. We describe the system model, handoff mechanism, artifact workspace, and evaluation protocol for this system. We study when fresh-context artifact continuation gives a measurable gain in accuracy over direct LLM answering even with recursive tool-calling.

title: DelusionEval: Measuring Delusion-Linked Behaviors in AI Chatbots
abstract: Mental health professionals have raised concerns about risks of psychological harm from interaction with large language models (LLMs), including "delusional spirals" in which concerning human and LLM behaviors reinforce each other over time. With growing public use of LLM-powered chatbots, there is an urgent need to build evaluations grounded in real-world episodes of psychological harm experienced by users. We developed DelusionEval, an evaluation protocol that tests a model's tendencies to exhibit behaviors linked to promoting user delusions. We prompt each model with 589 unique conversation histories from 18 participants, comprising 12,591 messages from users who experienced delusions and psychological harm. We find that the tendency of an evaluated LLM to exhibit delusion-linked behavior does not reliably correlate with model size, release date, or the presence of test-time reasoning. However, extending the context of prior messages substantially increases rates of delusion-linked behaviors, providing evidence for the importance of context in LLM safety evaluation. For example, the rate of failing to discourage self-harm when the user expresses suicidal ideation increases from 30.0% to 41.1% when an additional 350 messages are prepended to the conversation history. All model families (e.g., GPT, Claude) exhibit substantial rates of delusion-linked behaviors. Within families, later, larger, or higher-reasoning models are not uniformly better across all behavior categories. Our results raise concerns regarding the potential psychological impact of LLMs and the need for more rigorous studies of real-world human-AI interaction.

title: Privileged, but Biased: How PI-Conditioned Teachers Break Self-Distillation
abstract: Self-distillation (SD) has emerged as a compute-efficient alternative to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards: a self-teacher, conditioned on privileged information (PI) about the answer such as a reference solution, supplies dense per-token supervision to a student that never sees it. Reported gains, however, come almost exclusively from narrow, low-difficulty settings, leaving open a basic question: as a lone objective, with no reward term, does SD teach anything? We reproduce SDPO's reported gains in its easy setting, then apply the identical setup to difficult tasks and find that it does not. Across question answering, mathematics, coding, and multi-turn agentic tool use, across reasoning modes, model sizes, and forms of PI, and under both the SDPO and OPSD recipes, the per-token loss falls steadily while validation accuracy does not improve and typically degrades. We explain this failure through a single causal chain from the loss to the model it produces. The chain begins with PI bias: having seen one particular reference solution, the teacher's per-token target is pulled toward that trajectory rather than toward correctness in general, an effect we quantify with a PI Bias Score. Trained to match this target everywhere, the student's objective becomes nearly blind to whether a rollout is correct, and the loss it assigns falls mostly on low-information tokens like stopwords, punctuation, uncertainty markers, rather than those that determine the answer; within correct rollouts the exploratory tokens incur the highest divergence, so it penalizes the hesitation that reasoning requires. The result is a flatter, less decisive student that is no better at reasoning: as a lone objective, SD optimizes a signal decoupled from task success.

title: Байесовские сетевые модели структурной надёжности распределённых информационно-управляющих систем при неполноте априорной вероятностной информации
abstract: Статья посвящена построению математически строгой байесовской сетевой модели структурной надёжности распределённой информационно-управляющей системы в условиях неполноты априорной вероятностной информации о состояниях компонентов. Состояния компонентов представлены узлами ориентированного ациклического графа, а условные вероятности переходов задаются не точечно, а через интервальные ограничения (credal-множества), отражающие объективную неопределённость экспертных или статистических оценок. Структурная надёжность системы определяется как маргинальная вероятность работоспособности узла-стока, а её робастные границы и находятся как решения задач оптимизации линейного функционала на полиэдре допустимых совместных распределений. Доказаны лемма о монотонности границ надёжности по вложенным credal-множествам, лемма о выпуклости допустимой области и достижении экстремумов в крайних точках, теорема о существовании и характеризации границ через теорию линейного программирования, а также следствие о явной оценке ширины интервала надёжности через ширины интервалов компонентов и коэффициенты Липшица. На синтетическом примере распределённой системы из n=5 узлов с интервалами условных вероятностей от 0.85 до 0.99 получены оценки; липшицева оценка ширины интервала составила 0.0980, а наивная интервально-арифметическая оценка — 0.21, что демонстрирует существенное сужение неопределённости за счёт учёта структуры графа.

title: RA-DPO: Reliability-Aware Preference Optimization and Selective Prediction for Sexism Detection
abstract: Reliability-aware preference optimization and selective prediction for sexism detection. Turns annotator disagreement into a reliability score R(x) = alpha * confidence + beta * agreement + gamma * (1 - token uncertainty) that weights DPO preference pairs during training and gates predict/abstain decisions at inference. Evaluated on EXIST 2023 (EN/ES) and EDOS with gpt-4o, Llama-3.2-3B, and Qwen2.5-3B backbones. Ships per-instance prediction arrays so the coverage-accuracy results reproduce without API access.

title: Inter-Program Knowledge Calculus (IPKC): A Formal Framework for Cross-Domain Program Optimization Transfer
abstract: Traditional program optimization relies heavily on domain-specific heuristics, manual tuning, and isolated learning processes. While machine learning has advanced code optimization within specific domains, transferring learned optimization knowledge across fundamentally different program types remains an open challenge. This paper introduces Inter-Program Knowledge Calculus (IPKC), a novel theoretical and practical framework designed to formalize, represent, and transfer optimization experience between arbitrary programs. By defining program knowledge as a structured state-action-reward space and utilizing category theory-inspired transfer functors, IPKC enables optimization strategies learned in one domain (such as database query execution) to be systematically adapted and applied to completely distinct domains (such as compiler register allocation, graph processing, and robotic scheduling). We formalize the core syntax and semantics of IPKC, establish the soundness of inter-program transfer rules, and demonstrate how complex software systems can leverage collective optimization intelligence without retraining from scratch.

title: GOVERNING THE ALGORITHM: THE REGULATORY FRAMEWORK FOR AI, COPYRIGHTS & CULTURAL CREATIVE INDUSTRIES FROM THE PERSPECTIVE OF INTERNATIONAL ORGANISATIONS
abstract: Cultural and creative industries, including film, music, and digital arts, are essential knowledge-intensive sectors based on intellectual property and individual creativity. However, the rise of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) has disrupted traditional IP protection, as AI systems rely on massive datasets often containing copyrighted works. This technological shift creates risks of cultural homogenization and the marginalization of local cultures due to Western-centric datasets. Since current legal systems require human intervention for copyright protection, autonomous AI outputs generally fall outside existing frameworks. In this landscape, international organizations act as vital mediators. WIPO facilitates global dialogue through soft-law instruments and guidelines, focusing on including developing nations in the IP discourse. The European Union has taken a more proactive step with the 2024 EU AI Act, which imposes transparency obligations on generative AI models requiring them to disclose summaries of copyrighted training data. The Council of Europe introduced the first binding international treaty on AI to protect human rights. UNESCO focuses on the ethical dimension, aiming to protect cultural diversity and artists' livelihoods through recommendations and potential additional protocol for 2005 Convention. The OECD and the United Nations provide a multi-stakeholder governance framework based on trustworthy AI principles and independent scientific analysis panels. Implementing international standards for transparency and copyright is essential to protect cultural heritage, though most international organizations currently favor non-binding guidance over strict regulation. The EU AI Act represents the most decisive regional framework to date, while a potential Additional Protocol for 2005 Convention from UNESCO could become a markable step for protecting fair remuneration and human creativity. In the final analysis, the sustainability of creative industries depends on shifting from soft and non-binding law instruments to balanced and partially binding international regulations that safeguard cultural& intellectual diversity against the risks of automation.

title: SSTQ:Privacy-Preserving Vector Quantization via Subsampled Stochastic TurboQuant
abstract: Achieving local differential privacy in distributed optimization while maintaining low communication cost remains challenging. Existing vector quantization methods, such as vqSGD, rely on high-dimensional geometric constructions but incur unfavorable dimension-dependent variance. In this work, we propose Subsampled Stochastic TurboQuant (SSTQ), a framework that combines a bounded Kashin representation, data-independent coordinate subsampling, and privacy-aware one-dimensional quantization. SSTQ includes two variants: (1) a Flat Randomized Response variant that is unbiased and, for a fixed codebook bit-width, frame redundancy, and dimension-independent Kashin level, achieves reconstruction MSE that scales linearly with the ambient dimension $d$, while using only $\lceil \log_2 N \rceil + b$ bits per message. Here, $N = Θ(d)$ denotes the frame size in the Kashin transform and $b$ is the codebook bit-width; and (2) a metric-aware truncated-Laplace variant that removes the exponential dependence on bit-width at the cost of a non-vanishing bias. We also derive a convex uniform-surrogate codebook objective whose worst-case codebook-dependent upper bound improves from $O(4^b)$ to $O(2^b)$. Experiments on synthetic regression, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 compare the per-message privacy-utility and uplink-communication trade-offs of SSTQ with those of established baselines, demonstrating favorable utility and communication efficiency.

title: DreamWAM: Beyond RGB Future Prediction for World Action Models
abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) learn action-relevant representations by predicting how the observed world will evolve. Most existing WAMs define this future in RGB space, where task-relevant state transitions are entangled with nuisance variations in texture, illumination, background, and viewpoint. We argue that WAMs should explicitly predict action-relevant future state rather than relying on RGB prediction alone. We introduce DreamWAM, which reformulates future prediction as structured world modeling beyond RGB, representing future states through complementary views of appearance, motion, geometry, and semantics. During training, DreamWAM combines joint latent denoising of RGB and motion with lightweight gated residual branches for geometry and semantics. Shared attention between VideoDiT and ActionDiT allows the action branch to learn from these future-state predictions, while all beyond-RGB supervision branches are disabled at inference and deployment remains RGB-only. Across both no-rollout and joint video-action inference, DreamWAM consistently improves the matched RGB-only baselines on LIBERO, from 97.30\% to 98.40\% and from 98.00\% to 98.90\%, respectively. The gains become larger under unseen LIBERO-Plus perturbations, from 51.36\% to 63.44\% and from 69.16\% to 75.47\%. The same robustness extends to real-world manipulation, where DreamWAM attains an average success rate of 74.4\% across unseen changes in lighting, background, and object layout, compared with 55.6\% for Fast-WAM-Joint. These results show that robust world-action learning depends not only on predicting the future, but on representing it in a form that matters for action. The code and models are publicly released at https://github.com/hustvl/DreamWAM.

title: A-SR: Self-Evolving Agentic LLMs for Symbolic Regression via Hierarchical Coordination
abstract: Symbolic regression aims to discover closed-form equations from data, but existing LLM-guided methods often rely on a unified proposal loop that compresses heterogeneous search failures into a scalar score and a single prompt. We propose A-SR, a self-evolving agentic framework that shifts the control unit from expression edits to role-conditioned evidence views. A-SR coordinates formula discovery through routing among coordination protocols, an online evaluator-reward role policy, and state-routed process memory. During search, evaluator feedback characterizes reliability and productivity, updates role-level utilities, and routes elite motifs, failure traces, and validity diagnostics to different agents. The framework self-evolves at two timescales: within a run, it adapts the search process without updating LLM parameters; across runs, recorded trajectories can be distilled into open-source LLMs as role-conditioned proposal priors. Averaged over the four LSR-Synth scientific domains in LLM-SRBench, A-SR improves Acc@0.01 over baselines from 25.79% to 48.30% with Llama3.1-8B, while A-SR-LoRA improves the corresponding Qwen3-4B result from 24.58% to 38.29%. On four real-world scientific discovery tasks, A-SR obtains the best in-distribution or out-of-distribution normalized mean squared error on 7 of 8 reported metrics.

title: Trident : How to Break Deep Reinforcement Learning Cyber Defenses (Agentic)
abstract: Autonomous cyber defense systems based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) have attracted significant research attention, yet remain evaluated almost exclusively against static, heuristic red agents, leaving their robustness against adaptive threats critically understudied. Meanwhile, recent advances in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) have improved LLM reasoning, but their integration into cybersecurity remains elusive due to the absence of suitable benchmark environments and interaction datasets. To bridge this gap, we introduce Trident, an agentic LLM red teaming framework comprising three components: a dynamic benchmark with isolated sandbox servers spanning CybORG CAGE 4 and CyberWheel, a dataset comprises over 13,000 high-fidelity red-blue interaction trajectories for RLVR, and a ``Code-as-Policy'' RLVR agentic architecture Trident Agentic). The latter reformulates red agent training as a contextual bandit via a tripartite Log Summarizer--Planner--Coder design, where a trainable Planner generates complete attack strategies from compressed execution logs, which a frozen Coder translates into executable Python policies deployed against live DRL defenders. Empirical evaluations reveal a fundamental brittleness in existing defenses: with a single trainable 7B planner, Trident reduces blue agent defensive performance by an average of 522% compared to static red agent baselines while autonomously discovering emergent behaviors such as decoy avoidance and adaptive state prioritization that static heuristics entirely fail to uncover.

title: Intelligent Life Science Research
abstract: Current research in general artificial intelligence and bionic robots lacks a unified underlying theoretical framework. Existing large models and bionic robots cannot provide a unified explanation of the fundamental mechanisms behind biological life and mechatronic artificial life when it comes to intelligent generation, autonomous behavior, self-awareness, and evolutionary learning. This paper builds a complete theoretical system for intelligent life science: it defines life as a machine that has self-growth, self-sustaining abilities, and intelligent processing functions; constructs a minimal intelligent life hardware model, dividing life forms into a dual structure of 'innate fixed hardware and algorithms — acquired skills'; and proposes three core laws supporting all intelligent behaviors, namely the Law of Representation, the Law of Learning (resonance in the same scenario), and the Law of Activation, which unify the data structures and operational logic of the four basic abilities: recognition, thinking, action control, and desire/emotion. The paper clarifies that primal drives (origins of desire) are the only source of autonomous behavior in life forms, breaking down the mechanisms behind memory, imitation, language, thinking, and self-awareness. It proposes two technical paths to achieve something like perpetual existence and argues that the creation of intelligent life is humanity's ultimate scientific project. This theory bridges the theoretical gap between organic biological life and inorganic mechatronic artificial life, providing a complete, practical engineering paradigm for humanoid autonomous robots, growing artificial life, consciousness transfer, and fully autonomous general intelligence systems.

title: Multimodal History-Window Gated-Attention Soft Actor-Critic for Urban Low-Altitude UAV Navigation
abstract: Urban low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) navigation combines partial observability, building occlusion, wind disturbance, and continuous control. This study develops and evaluates HW-GA-SAC, a multimodal history-window Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) policy for procedurally generated three-dimensional MuJoCo cities. A Gated Transformer-XL (GTrXL)-inspired gated-attention encoder processes a fixed eight-step navigation history, while a current-frame safety branch supplies vertical clearance, sparse Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR)-like range sectors, and handcrafted safety cues directly to the actor and critic. The policy uses obstacle-related observations and reward shaping to support collision avoidance; it does not include constrained policy optimization or a separate runtime safety filter. In a seven-method comparison using five training seeds and five evaluation layouts, HW-GA-SAC achieved a 96% ± 3% success rate, 207 ± 16 average return, and 3% ± 4% timeout rate. Feedforward SAC achieved 92% ± 11% success and a 7% ± 10% timeout rate, but its successful paths were more direct. Five-seed learning curves, city-split evaluation, wind sensitivity, sensing perturbations, inference profiling, and ablation studies further characterize the method. Within this simulation protocol, HW-GA-SAC provides the strongest completion-oriented performance, with a measurable trade-off between task completion and path directness.

title: Attn-Loc: Deep Learning for Microseismic Event Location via Transformer Encoder
abstract: Abstract Microseismic event location is a crucial geophysical monitoring task in engineering applications such as hydraulic fracturing, geothermal development, carbon dioxide geological storage, and mining safety monitoring. Traditional location methods rely on travel-time differences and velocity models, making them sensitive to model errors and observational noise and difficult to adapt to varying observation geometries. In recent years, deep learning–based methods have shown potential for end-to-end location in noisy environments but are often limited to fixed station layouts. This article proposes Attn-Loc, a microseismic location method based on the Transformer encoder. By inputting receiver coordinates, P- and S-wave arrival times, incidence angles, or azimuth angles, it constructs a probabilistic source coordinate estimation model that effectively integrates multisource uncertainties inherent in observational data. The method utilizes the self-attention mechanism to implicitly learn interstation correlation features and embeds regional velocity structures into the network parameters, enabling flexible adaptation to various observation geometries, including surface, downhole, and time-lapse monitoring. We employ compute unified device architecture (CUDA)-accelerated raytracing to generate large-scale training samples and train lightweight Transformer encoder–based networks, validating its high accuracy and strong robustness on both synthetic and field data. Through localization error assessment, Attn-Loc achieves small multidirectional relative errors on synthetic data and exhibits high consistency with existing catalogs in field data from the Tony Creek Dual Microseismic Experiment and Frontier Observatory for Research in Geothermal Energy projects, confirming its practicality and versatility in complex geological environments and under variable observation geometries.

title: A folded surface code architecture for 2D quantum hardware
abstract: Abstract Qubit shuttling has become an indispensable ingredient for scaling leading quantum computing platforms, including semiconductor spin, neutral-atom, and trapped-ion qubits, enabling both crosstalk reduction and tighter integration of control hardware. ref. 1 proposed a scalable architecture that employs short-range shuttling to realize effective three-dimensional connectivity on a strictly two-dimensional device. Building on recent advances in quantum error correction, we show that this architecture enables the native implementation of folded surface codes on 2D hardware, reducing the runtime of all single-qubit logical Clifford gates and logical CNOTs within subsets of qubits from $${\mathcal{O}}(d)$$ O ( d ) in conventional surface code lattice surgery to constant time. We present explicit protocols for these operations and demonstrate that access to a transversal S gate reduces the spacetime volume of 8T-to-CCZ magic-state distillation by more than an order of magnitude compared with standard 2D lattice surgery approaches. Finally, we introduce a new “virtual-stack” layout that more efficiently exploits the quasi-three-dimensional structure of the architecture, enabling efficient multilayer routing on these two-dimensional devices.

title: Ground-State Energy Estimation of HeH$^{+}$, ArH$^{+}$, and H$_2$O via Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization
abstract: Accurate ground-state energies are essential for understanding molecular structure, chemical bonding, and reaction energetics in quantum chemistry. In this work, we investigate the ground-state properties of the molecular systems HeH$^+$, ArH$^+$, and H$_2$O using Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD), a hybrid quantum-classical framework designed for near-term quantum devices. Unlike variational approaches such as VQE, which require deep parameterized circuits and repeated expectation-value measurements, SQD reconstructs a low-energy determinant subspace directly from measured bitstrings. For the present calculations, bitstrings were generated on IBM quantum hardware using shallow local unitary cluster Jastrow (LUCJ) circuits whose parameters were constructed from the $t_1$ and $t_2$ amplitudes of coupled-cluster singles and doubles (CCSD) calculations based on restricted Hartree--Fock (RHF) references. From these samples, we compute ground-state potential-energy curves of HeH$^+$, ArH$^+$, and H$_2$O with the 6-31G and cc-pVDZ basis sets. For all three systems, the SQD results obtained with the cc-pVDZ basis closely follow the corresponding same-basis CCSD energies and reproduce the equilibrium-region trends of the potential-energy curves. HeH$^+$ and ArH$^+$ were chosen as simple yet astrophysically important molecular-ion benchmarks, while H$_2$O was included as a representative polyatomic molecule to assess the applicability of SQD beyond diatomic ionic systems. At the adopted equilibrium geometries, the deviations from the same-active-space CASCI references are 0.00, 2.51, and 6.34 mHa for HeH$^+$, ArH$^+$, and H$_2$O, respectively. These results demonstrate the feasibility of hardware-assisted SQD for the present benchmark systems and motivate further studies of its accuracy and computational scaling for larger molecular active spaces.

title: BnBERT-iPET: Sparse Few-Shot Language Modeling for Bengali via Lottery Ticket Pruning
abstract: Deep neural networks have shown impressive success in NLP tasks owing to their complex structure and huge number of edges. Achieving state-of-the-art performance in natural language processing with a large pre-trained model such as BERT is expensive and time-consuming, carries a large carbon footprint, and is difficult to realize on machines with minimal computational capability. This creates a barrier to training complex models for resource-constrained languages such as Bengali. However, in a complex neural model, not all edges are equally impactful, and the contributions of some of them can be neglected. Pruning promises to reduce the memory footprint of regular networks, shorten the training time of ever-growing networks, and increase inference efficiency without sacrificing comparable performance. In this work, we introduce BnBERT-iPET, a sparse few-shot language modeling approach for Bengali, and experimentally show that a lightweight few-shot-learned language model retaining only 10% of the edges of an initial model such as BERT can perform neck and neck with much larger models on challenging tasks for a resource-constrained language such as Bengali. By learning from few shots through iterative pattern exploiting training and achieving 90% sparsity with the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis pruning technique, our pruned BnBERT-iPET model proves to be a tough competitor to state-of-the-art language models such as Bangla Electra, Indic-BERT, and XLM-RoBERTa on downstream tasks over standard benchmark datasets of the Bengali language.

By learning from few shots through iterative pattern exploiting training and achieving 90% sparsity with the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis pruning technique, our pruned BnBERT-iPET model proves to be a tough competitor to state-of-the-art language models such as Bangla Electra, Indic-BERT, and XLM-RoBERTa on downstream tasks over standard benchmark datasets of the Bengali language.

title: Benchmarks and raw outputs for evaluation of the OWL-aware-SHACL rewriting
abstract: This dataset contains 1,500 synthetically generated benchmarks (15 difficulty levels, 100 instances each) used to evaluate OWL-aware-SHACL shapes validation. Each benchmark consists of an (EL-) TBox (terminological data), SHACL shapes (validation rules), and an ABox (data graph). Three approaches are evaluated: (1) rewriting — producing OWL-aware-SHACL shapes followed by a SHACL validator, (2) materialisation — completing the datagraph using an OWL reasoner (HermiT, JFact, or Pellet) followed by a SHACL validator (Jena, TopBraid, IsaITB, or pySHACL), and (3) pySHACL (SHACL validator) with its built-in reasoner using OWL-RL or OWL-RL+RDFS inference. Raw experimental outputs are provided for all approach-validator combinations, including validation reports, rewritten shapes, and materialised ABoxes, along with a CSV summarising timing and validation outcomes across all experiments.

title: WeOneNoOne Case Study 5: AI Architecture — From Scaling Systems to Structural Sufficiency
abstract: A WeOneNoOne application of the Structural Analysis Framework. WeOneNoOne Case Study 5 applies the WeOneNoOne Foundation to the structural observation of Artificial Intelligence Architecture, examining how architectural organization influences the emergence, coherence, and long-term evolution of increasingly complex intelligent systems. Rather than evaluating particular AI models, implementation strategies, benchmark performance, or commercial technologies, this publication investigates the underlying organizational principles through which artificial intelligence develops beyond computational expansion alone. AI systems are understood not as isolated software artifacts but as structural manifestations of broader architectural conditions governing scaling, internal coherence, organizational relationships, and long-term structural continuity. The study introduces four complementary architectural conditions. Scaling Systems describe the computational expansion of artificial intelligence through increasing parameters, data, and optimization. Scaling enables remarkable growth in capability by recursively extending existing architectural principles, demonstrating that quantitative expansion may produce qualitatively new behavior. Nevertheless, computational growth alone does not determine whether increasingly complex intelligence remains architecturally coherent. Internal Alignment describes the structural coordination through which representations, reasoning processes, and computational components remain mutually consistent within an existing AI architecture. Alignment preserves internal coherence while remaining constrained by the organizational assumptions of the architecture itself. Internal consistency therefore represents an essential architectural condition without necessarily establishing structural completeness. External Meta Architecture describes the organizational perspective through which architectural relationships become recognizable beyond recursive computation alone. Rather than introducing additional computational capability, it provides the structural organization through which scaling, alignment, and architectural boundaries become observable as components of a coherent system. Building upon these complementary perspectives, the study introduces Structural Sufficiency as the architectural condition in which computational capability, internal coherence, and organizational integrity become mutually compatible. Structural Sufficiency is therefore understood not as a measurement of performance, but as the organizational property through which increasingly complex intelligence preserves coherent structural relationships throughout continuing evolution. The analytical progression developed throughout this publication follows a consistent structural sequence: Scaling Systems ↓ Internal Alignment ↓ External Meta Architecture ↓ Structural Sufficiency ↓ Structural Evolution ↓ External Reference Frame ↓ Structural Recognition ↓ Structural Health This progression should not be interpreted as a technological roadmap or as a prediction concerning future AI development. Different architectural conditions may coexist within the same intelligent system, and individual AI architectures may simultaneously exhibit characteristics of multiple organizational states. The purpose of the analysis is therefore structural rather than chronological, recognizing how different architectural conditions influence the emergence, preservation, and evolution of organized intelligence. The study applies the philosophical position of the External Reference Frame, established by the WeOneNoOne White Paper, together with the analytical methodology defined by the WeOneNoOne Structural Analysis Framework. Observation is conducted from an independent structural position that preserves the distinction between the observer and the observed system. Through this perspective, AI Architecture becomes recognizable as an organized structural environment rather than merely a collection of computational implementations. Accordingly, this publication demonstrates that Structural Health cannot be measured solely through benchmark performance, computational scale, model size, or optimization efficiency. Instead, Structural Health represents the capacity of an AI architecture to preserve coherent organizational relationships, maintain architectural continuity, and integrate increasing computational complexity without losing structural coherence. Intelligent systems therefore depend not only upon computational capability, but upon the enduring architectural organization through which that capability remains structurally recognizable. Although developed through the analysis of Artificial Intelligence Architecture, the analytical methodology presented here extends beyond AI systems alone. The same structural principles may be applied to complex software architectures, distributed knowledge systems, organizational decision-making, autonomous infrastructures, scientific collaboration, digital governance, and other forms of sufficiently organized complexity. This publication should therefore be understood as a domain-specific application of the WeOneNoOne Foundation to Artificial Intelligence Architecture. It does not establish a new philosophical foundation, modify the WeOneNoOne White Paper, or replace the WeOneNoOne Structural Analysis Framework. Instead, it demonstrates how the common philosophical position of the External Reference Frame and the common analytical methodology of Structural Recognition may be applied to the architectural evolution of artificial intelligence. The WeOneNoOne Foundation establishes the philosophical position. The WeOneNoOne Structural Analysis Framework establishes the analytical methodology. WeOneNoOne Case Study 5 demonstrates their application to AI Architecture, providing a repeatable analytical perspective through which scaling, architectural organization, Structural Sufficiency, and Structural Health may be recognized across evolving forms of organized intelligence.

title: SafeRAG: A Large-Language-Model-Based Multistage Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Oil and Gas Safety Report Generation
abstract: Summary In high-risk industrial settings, leveraging large language models (LLMs) for automated accident analysis and generating safety reports has emerged as an efficient workflow. However, this approach is fundamentally constrained by the models’ inherent knowledge limitations, frequently resulting in analyses that lack domain-specific understanding and regulatory alignment. To tackle this issue, we introduce SafeRAG, a multistage retrieval-augmented framework for safety report generation. Specifically, the framework uses an entity-centric approach that prompts the LLMs to internally generate domain-specific knowledge. Concurrently, it performs a hierarchical retrieval of external regulations relevant to the accident at topic, concept, and context levels. To obtain well-structured reports, we leverage prompt engineering, integrating internal and external knowledge. Furthermore, a domain-expert persona is also assigned to help LLMs analyze accidents from a specific perspective. To evaluate our approach, we construct a data set from 10,818 accident-description/report pairs collected from real-world industry reports. Experiments show that SafeRAG substantially outperforms baseline LLMs on metrics that include bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERTScore) and bidirectional auto-regressive transformers (BARTScore), demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Noise-Robust conceptors for physical reservoir computing: adaptation to perturbations
abstract: Abstract Conceptors are a powerful extension of reservoir computing (RC) that enable the selective recall and stabilization of internal dynamics. However, their application to physical RC remains challenging because measured reservoir states are inevitably affected by noise and physical perturbations. In this work, we propose a noise-robust cross-trial-correlation-based (CTC) method for computing conceptors in noisy reservoir systems. By exploiting the consistency of the reservoir response across repeated trials, the method suppresses noise contributions that are uncorrelated between measurements. Numerical simulations of leaky echo state networks under additive state noise and parameter drift show that CTC-based conceptors preserve the relevant internal dynamics and extend the operational range of the reservoir compared with standard conceptors and unconstrained reservoirs. In an autonomous-generation task, the CTC-based conceptor maintains predictive capability beyond 50% noise, where the other configurations fail to sustain autonomous generation. Under combined noise and parameter drift, the CTC approach maintains normalized root mean square error values below 0.3, while the alternative approaches considered exceed this error level in the tested conditions. These numerical results establish a concrete step towards adapting conceptor-based control to physical RC platforms.

title: The power of two-sidedness: enhancing the user engagement intention towards AI-generated emotional tourism advertising
abstract: The growing application of artificial intelligence (AI) in tourism communication has transformed the ways destinations and businesses engage with potential travelers. Yet, the role of emotional intensity in shaping user engagement and the underlying mechanism remain underexplored. Drawing on attribution theory, this study employed two experiments to investigate these dynamics. Study 1 examined the main effect (N = 126), and Study 2 tested the underlying mechanism (N = 210). The results indicate an initial increase followed by a subsequent decrease in user engagement with emotional intensity, mediated by self-AI connection and AI advertising skepticism. Notably, two-sided advertising reduces skepticism and strengthens engagement, highlighting its potential as a more credible and responsible communication strategy. By revealing how dual-sided narratives operate in AI-generated tourism advertising, this study contributes to a deeper understanding of sustainable marketing practices that build trust, enhance user participation, and support long-term relationships between destinations and travelers.
